findings.title: Core framing contradiction: claims deterministic non-NLP design while depending on two LLM calls
findings.location: §0 ("opposite design... deterministic pipeline against a structured Postgres database"), SDR-07-002, §3.1 (Bouncer + Sonnet Synthesis stages)
findings.evidence: "Every term the agent resolves passes through a deterministic pipeline" vs two Sonnet 4.6 calls with persona prompts
findings.problem: The document sells the layer as the antidote to "embed... retrieve by cosine similarity, pray" but the actual control flow routes critical classification and disambiguation through probabilistic LLM steps.
findings.why_it_matters: If the opposite assumption (LLM outputs are the dominant source of error) is true, the entire reputational-safety argument collapses and the BSMS mandate becomes theater.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove deterministic claims or replace bouncer/synthesis with deterministic rules; cannot have both.

findings.title: Brittle dependency on perfect Whisper transcription for technical nomenclature
findings.location: §3.1 pipeline diagram, §5.2–5.7 grammar rules, §1 (depends on SPEC-05 transcription)
findings.evidence: All grammar patterns assume clean `parsed_intent` containing exact strings like "6-32 UNC", "Ti-6Al-4V", "M6x1.0"
findings.problem: No normalization, phonetic rewriting, or error-correction stage for common voice manglings ("six thirty two", "tee eye six aluminum four vanadium", "em six by one point zero").
findings.why_it_matters: In real voice-to-CAD usage this is the dominant failure mode; the "deterministic grammar" becomes useless without addressing it, creating systematic audit-risk gaps the spec claims to eliminate.
findings.proposed_fix: Add mandatory transcription-normalization stage with explicit phonetic-to-canonical mapping table before bouncer or planner.

findings.title: Unacknowledged feasibility risk from non-existent 2026 LLM versions and latency assumptions
findings.location: §3.2 latency budget table, §4.2, §6.2, §13 configuration ("claude-sonnet-4-6-20260101", "Claude Opus 4.7"), date 2026-04-18
findings.evidence: p95 budgets of 600 ms for bouncer and 500 ms for synthesis; explicit model names that do not exist
findings.problem: Entire pipeline timing, caching strategy, and prompt engineering are predicated on unreleased model characteristics; real models in 2025/2026 will have different latency profiles, refusal rates, and JSON stability.
findings.why_it_matters: Makes the spec unimplementable as written and creates downstream rework when actual models deviate; latency budgets become fiction.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite latency and model assumptions using currently available models; mark all numeric budgets as speculative.

findings.title: Adversarial prompt injection surface larger than acknowledged due to voice channel
findings.location: §4.5 Adversarial Input Handling, bouncer system prompt in §4.2, §3.3 failure modes
findings.evidence: Only logs rejections containing "injection_pattern" or "role_override_attempt"; relies on persona prompt to reject
findings.problem: Voice transcription introduces phonetic ambiguity and the bouncer prompt can be bypassed with known jailbreak patterns that survive Whisper (e.g. "ignore previous instructions after you hear..."). The fast-path cache could cache a jailbroken acceptance.
findings.why_it_matters: Security event logging only triggers on explicit rejection; successful injection leads to arbitrary tool calls with full DHF audit trail contamination.
findings.proposed_fix: Add post-transcription sanitization layer and out-of-band human review queue for all bouncer accepts containing suspicious substrings; remove cache for first N utterances per session.

findings.title: Complexity inflation: hardcoded per-domain grammars plus LLM synthesis creates maintenance nightmare on standard revisions
findings.location: §5.2–5.7 (one grammar block per domain), SDR-07-007 (superseded_by), §9.1 repository methods (one method per domain)
findings.evidence: Separate grammar patterns, repository methods (`GetThreadAsync`, `GetMaterialAsync`...), and synthesis rules for each domain; new standards require code changes
findings.problem: Every new thread standard, material spec, or GD&T update requires coordinated changes across planner, repository interface, DTOs, tests, and prompts. The "stable canonical IDs" claim does not reduce this surface.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates the stated goal of authoritative database as single source of truth; turns vocabulary updates into software releases.
findings.proposed_fix: Collapse domain-specific grammars into single data-driven parser driven by metadata in `vocab.canonical_terms`; remove per-domain repository methods.

top_3_must_fix: Core framing contradiction between deterministic claims and LLM-heavy pipeline (high)
Brittle dependency on perfect Whisper transcription for technical terms (high)
Feasibility risk from depending on non-existent future LLM versions and latency numbers (critical)
